I have been farming this same land in Quzhou for more than fifty years. My husband passed several years ago, and my children went to work in the city. I manage about five mu myself, with my son coming back during harvest to help, and I hire the machine station for the big jobs like plowing and combining — my back cannot do what it once could.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize, same as always, same as my neighbors. That is the rotation here. I know wheat. I know maize. I do not take risks on new crops at my age. I plant wheat in October after the rains slow, and after we cut wheat in June I plant maize immediately on the stubble. The same five mu does double duty each year.

For wheat I use the variety the village seed shop has sold for years — I know it does well on my soil. I put down the same fertilizer my neighbors use: a bag of compound fertilizer at sowing, then urea when the weather warms in spring. For water I irrigate before winter sets in to protect the roots, then again at jointing, and once more when the grain is filling — three times is what I have always done. I spray twice: once in spring for aphids, once for rust if I see the orange spots.

For summer maize I buy the hybrid seed in bags from the co-op, same brand as last year. Maize here gets summer rain so I only irrigate once if July is dry. I fertilize once at sowing and once when the stalks are knee-high. I spray once for corn borer.

My yields are not the best in the village, but they are steady and I am not wasting money.
